title: Grammar: Discourse Markers in Spoken English
grammarTip:
Дискурсивные маркеры в разговорной речи — устная речь богаче письменной:

ПОДТВЕРЖДЕНИЕ:
Right · OK · Sure · Exactly · Absolutely · Indeed · Precisely

НАЧАЛО ОТВЕТА / РАЗМЫШЛЕНИЯ:
Well... · So... · Actually... · Basically... · You know...
"Well, that's an interesting question." · "So, what I think is..."

СМЕНА ТЕМЫ:
Anyway · By the way · Incidentally · Speaking of which · On another note
"Anyway, back to the main point..." · "By the way, did you know...?"

ВЫРАЖЕНИЕ HESITATION (паузы):
You know... · I mean... · Let me see... · How can I put it...

💡 В разговорной английской речи эти маркеры звучат естественно.
В академическом тексте — избегай "you know", "basically", "anyway"!

grammarTable.subject: Hedges
grammarTable.verb: kind of / sort of / a bit / somewhat / rather
grammarTable.example: "It's kind of difficult to explain." / "I sort of see what you mean." / "That's a bit fast."

grammarTable.subject: Fillers
grammarTable.verb: well / um / uh / you know / I mean / like
grammarTable.example: "Well, I think the issue is..." / "You know, it's complicated." / "I mean, that's one way to look at it."

grammarTable.subject: Response tokens
grammarTable.verb: right / yeah / OK / exactly / indeed / of course

grammarTable.subject: Reformulators
grammarTable.verb: I mean / that is / in other words / or rather
grammarTable.example: "I mean, what I'm trying to say is..." / "Or rather, it's more like..." / "In other words..."

grammarTable.subject: Stance markers
grammarTable.verb: actually / basically / honestly / frankly / to be honest
grammarTable.example: "Actually, I disagree." / "Honestly, it was much harder." / "To be honest, I'm not sure."

grammarTable.subject: Topic managers
grammarTable.verb: anyway / so / right / now / by the way / speaking of which
grammarTable.short: shifting topic or returning to main point
grammarTable.example: "Anyway, the point is..." / "So, where were we?" / "By the way, have you heard about..."

rows.form: "Kind of / sort of" — informal softening
rows.example: "It's kind of hard to explain without an example." / "I sort of understand, but not fully."

rows.form: "A bit / a little" — minimal softening
rows.example: "That was a bit too fast for me." / "Could you speak a little more slowly?"

rows.form: "Somewhat / rather" — more formal alternatives
rows.example: "The explanation was somewhat unclear." / "I find this rather difficult."

rows.form: Use hedges to be polite, tentative, or approximate
rows.example: "She's sort of in charge." / "It was around five o'clock." / "He's a bit of a nervous speaker."

grammarExtra.title: Fillers: Managing the Floor in Spoken English

rows.form: "Well" — transitional; introducing a response or shift
rows.example: "Well, that's one way to look at it." / "Well, I'm not sure I agree."

rows.form: "You know" — assuming shared knowledge; seeking solidarity
rows.example: "You know what I mean, right?" / "It's just, you know, a bit complicated."

rows.form: "I mean" — clarifying or correcting what was just said
rows.example: "It was difficult — I mean, nearly impossible." / "I mean, that's not quite what I said."

rows.form: "Like" — informal: approximating, giving examples, quoting
rows.example: "She was like, totally confused." / "It's like a kind of signposting technique."

rows.form: "Right" / "I see" — acknowledgement
rows.example: Speaker A: "So the problem is the pace." Speaker B: "Right." (I understand)

rows.form: "Exactly" / "Precisely" — strong agreement
rows.example: "That's exactly what I was thinking." / "Precisely — the warrant is implicit."

rows.form: "Fair enough" — accepting a point even if not fully agreeing
rows.example: "Fair enough — I can see why you'd interpret it that way."

rows.form: "Mm" / "Uh-huh" — minimal responses — signalling continued attention
rows.example: Used during others' long turns to show you're listening without interrupting

rows.form: "Actually" — correcting, contradicting, or surprising
rows.example: "Actually, it's the other way around." / "I actually find it quite helpful."

rows.form: "Basically" — summarising or getting to the point
rows.example: "Basically, the problem is the lack of preparation." / "So basically, you need to slow down."

rows.form: "Honestly / Frankly / To be honest" — signalling candour
rows.example: "Honestly, I'm not sure what I'm doing." / "To be honest, that's a bit too fast."

rows.form: "Obviously / Clearly" — marking what should be evident
rows.example: "Obviously, more practice is needed." / "Clearly, this approach isn't working."

rows.form: "Anyway" — returning to main point or changing topic
rows.example: "Anyway, as I was saying…" / "Anyway, let's move on to the next point."

rows.form: "So" — transitioning or drawing a conclusion
rows.example: "So, to summarise…" / "So, what you're saying is…"

rows.form: "Right / OK" — marking a transition or checking in
rows.example: "Right, let's try that again." / "OK, so where were we?"

rows.form: "By the way" — introducing something less central
rows.example: "By the way, have you seen the reading list?" / "By the way, there's an extension available."

"The instruction was ___ unclear — I didn't fully understand the task." (softening)

exercises.hint: Hedging words soften a critical observation

exercises.text: Speaker A: "So the key is clarity." Speaker B: "___, that's what I found too."

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct topic manager.
exercises.text: "___, as I was saying — the main issue is pacing."
exercises.hint: "Anyway" or "So" = returning to the main point

exercises.instruction: Choose the best filler for buying thinking time.
exercises.text: "___, that's a really interesting question — let me think about it."
exercises.hint: "Well" is a classic transitional filler buying time before responding

exercises.text: "It was difficult — ___ ___, nearly impossible." (clarifying what you just said)
exercises.hint: "I mean" = clarifying or strengthening what was just said

exercises.text: "___, we need to practise more if we want to improve." (summarising)

exercises.instruction: Complete with an appropriate response token.
exercises.text: A: "The pause felt really long to me." B: "___ ___ — but it probably seemed normal to the audience."
exercises.hint: "Fair enough" = accepting a point without necessarily fully agreeing

opts: "Honestly, that was the best lecture I've ever attended — it was perfect."
"Honestly, I found parts of it quite difficult to follow."
"Honestly speaking, none of the above are wrong."
exercises.correct: "Honestly, I found parts of it quite difficult to follow."
exercises.hint: "Honestly" = signalling candour, often about something mildly negative or personal

exercises.text: "___ ___ ___, have you tried recording yourself to get feedback on your pacing?"
exercises.hint: "By the way" = introducing something not directly related to the main point

exercises.text: "You know what I mean? It's like it's almost there but not quite."
opts: Seeking confirmation that the listener understands
exercises.correct: Seeking confirmation that the listener understands
exercises.hint: "You know?" = "Do you understand what I mean?" — seeking solidarity

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct discourse marker.
exercises.text: "___, to get back to the main point — the most important strategy is pacing."
exercises.hint: "Anyway" or "So" returns to the main point after a digression

exercises.text: "The lecture was about prosodics — ___ ___, the rhythm and stress of spoken language."
exercises.hint: "In other words" = reformulating — explaining the same idea differently

exercises.instruction: Complete the dialogue with an appropriate minimal response.
exercises.text: A: "So I've been practising signposting every day now." B: "___, that's a great habit to develop."
exercises.hint: Minimal response acknowledging what was said and showing engagement

exercises.instruction: Which is NOT typically a discourse marker in spoken English?
exercises.hint: "Notwithstanding" is a formal written connector — not a spoken discourse marker

exercises.instruction: What function does "Right, let's move on" serve?
opts: Managing the topic — signalling a transition to the next point
exercises.correct: Managing the topic — signalling a transition to the next point
exercises.hint: "Right" as a topic manager = marking a transition or checking in

questions.text: "___, I think we're approaching this the wrong way." (gently correcting/surprising)
questions.hint: "Actually" = correcting, contradicting, or introducing a surprise

questions.text: "The explanation was ___ unclear — could you try a different approach?" (softening the criticism)
questions.correct: kind of / sort of / a bit
questions.hint: Hedging: "kind of / sort of / a bit" soften the criticism

questions.text: "___, the main problem is the pacing — you're rushing the key points." (getting to the point)
questions.hint: "Basically" = summarising or getting to the core of the issue

questions.text: "A: 'So the key insight is that communication repair matters most.' B: '___ — that's exactly what I've been finding.'" (strong agreement)
questions.hint: "Exactly / Precisely" = strong agreement with what was just said

questions.text: "___, as I was saying — repair strategies are the key." (returning to main point)
questions.hint: "Anyway" = returning to the main point after a digression

questions.text: "Notwithstanding" is a common spoken discourse marker.
questions.hint: "Notwithstanding" is a formal written connector, not a spoken discourse marker

questions.text: "___, I'm not completely sure about this — let me think." (signalling candour/honesty)
questions.hint: "Honestly / To be honest" = signalling candid speech

questions.text: "It was a bit fast — ___ ___, nearly impossible to follow." (clarifying)
questions.hint: "I mean" = clarifying or strengthening what was just said

questions.text: "___, that's one way to look at it — but let me explain why I see it differently." (transitional)
questions.hint: "Well" = transitional filler — acknowledging before introducing a different view

questions.text: "___ ___ ___, have you tried using signposting phrases in everyday conversation?" (off-topic addition)
questions.hint: "By the way" = introducing something not directly in the main flow

questions.text: "The issue is pacing — ___ ___ ___, the need to slow down deliberately." (reformulating)
questions.hint: "In other words" = reformulating the same idea more clearly

opts: Accepting a point — even if not fully agreeing
questions.correct: Accepting a point — even if not fully agreeing
questions.hint: "Fair enough" = conceding a point without full agreement
